prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

I love your lips when they’re wet with wine And red with a wild desire; I love your eyes when the lovelight lies Lit with a passionate fire. I love your arms when the warm white flesh Touches mine in a fond embrace; I love your hair when the strands enmesh Your kisses against my face. Not for me the cold, calm kiss Of a virgin’s bloodless love; Not for me the saint’s white bliss, Nor the heart of a spotless dove. But give me the love that so freely gives And laughs at the whole world’s blame, With your body so young and warm in my arms, It sets my poor heart aflame. So kiss me sweet with your warm wet mouth, Still fragrant with ruby wine, And say with a fervor born of the South That your body and soul are mine. Clasp me close in your warm young arms, While the pale stars shine above, And we’ll live our whole young lives away In the joys of a living love.

And declare with a fervor ardent and deep  
That your body and soul are mine.  

Hold me close in your tender embrace

outputs.L3:
Here is a complete, well-structured expansion of the bullet points, crafted as a passionate and cohesive prose piece:

***

Love, in its truest and most transcendent form, is not a quiet spark but an consuming flame. From the very beginning, the speaker is captivated by the breathtaking physical beauty of their beloved, drawn into an orbit governed by intense sensual attraction. The lover’s presence ignites a fiery passion—a dynamic, incandescent force that awakens every sense and demands to be recognized. 

In light of this consuming fire, the speaker explicitly rejects any notion of love that is chaste, lukewarm, or stoically restrained. To love with hesitation or under the guise of cold, calculated propriety is to diminish love’s true power. The speaker scorns the idea that affection should be measured or subdued, casting aside tepid emotional compromises in favor of a raw, unapologetic, and overwhelming desire.

This passion demands absolute freedom. The speaker calls for an uninhibited relationship—one that gives affection generously and openly, entirely unburdened by shame or doubt. In a world governed by strict social norms and watchful eyes, the lovers must build a sanctuary of their own, boldly disregarding societal judgment and the opinions of a cynical public. Their devotion is accountable only to itself, existing beyond the reach of conventional constraints.

Crucially, this bond is far more than a fleeting physical attraction; it is a plea for absolute intimacy. The speaker demands nothing less than the complete devotion of both body and soul. Half-measures and guarded hearts have no place here. It is an invitation to a total merging of existences, where physical desire and spiritual unity become indistinguishable, binding two lives together in complete surrender.

Ultimately, this fiery manifesto is driven by the urgent awareness that youth is fleeting. Rather than wasting precious years in timid anticipation or restrained decorum, the speaker longs to spend their youth fully immersed in the immediate, vibrant joys of a living love. Life is meant to be felt deeply in the present moment, and the speaker urges their lover to seize this vitality now—to burn brightly together while the morning of their lives is still theirs to command.
outputs.L4:
Here is an expansion of the summary into a complete, late-19th-century-style romantic poem:

***

### The Fire and the Wine

Let pious souls extol the quiet frost,  
And praise the pale, untroubled, marble grace;  
They count their hollow virtues, blind and lost,  
Locked in a cold and passionless embrace.  
I crave no saintly crown, no frozen prayer,  
No bloodless heaven built of shadow-light—  
I trade the icy stillness of the air  
For wilder wonders in the pulse of night.  

Give me the crimson stain upon your lip,  
Where heavy vintages of passion cling;  
From that sweet, breathless chalice let me sip,  
And taste the reckless joy the senses bring.  
Look on me with those eyes of sudden fire,  
Whose burning glances consume my mortal dread,  
And awaken in the dark a fierce desire  
That quickens every drop the gods have made.  

Fold me within the summer of your arms,  
Press heart to pounding heart and breath to breath;  
No distant code of virtue holds the charms  
That conquer time and mock the fear of death.  
Why trade the vivid ecstasy of flesh  
For promised air beyond the quiet skies?  
Here in the warm, entangled, velvet mesh,  
The only true divinity arises.  

Then yield to me! Yield body, heart, and soul—  
Withhold no secret ember from the flame!  
In total, shared surrender we are whole,  
Beyond the reach of judgment, law, or shame.  
Let hypocrites keep virtue’s lonely night;  
We hold the sun within a single kiss—  
For earth’s uninhibited, burning light  
Is richer far than all their promised bliss.
